title: What Happens If a Fish Swallows Your Hook?
hook: Inside a fish's throat, your swallowed hook can lodge deep in the esophagus.
script: Inside a fish's throat, your swallowed hook can lodge deep in the esophagus. Researchers call deep hooking perhaps the single biggest factor in whether a released fish dies. Rip it out, and in a study on bluegill, a sunfish cousin of bass, 44 percent died within ten days. When the line was cut instead, deaths dropped to about 12 percent, and most fish shed the hook on their own. So when your hook is swallowed, don't dig. Cut the line and let it go.

claims.text: A swallowed hook can lodge in the esophagus.
Deep hooking is perhaps the single most important factor in injury and death of released fish.
Bluegill and black bass are both in the sunfish family, Centrarchidae.
Largemouth bass are in the sunfish family, Centrarchidae.
In the bluegill study, 44 percent of deeply hooked fish died within 10 days when the hook was removed.
When the line was cut, mortality was about 12.5 percent after 10 days.
Most line-cut fish had expelled the hook within 10 days.
Cutting the line is a more effective release method than removing the hook for deeply hooked fish.
